newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - focus is on Singapore.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - focus is on Singapore.

text.p: Gulf oil product prices and traders will have little choice next week than to track developments in Singapore after recent sharp prices losses in Asia, traders in the region said on Thursday.
"After that performance, I'm not going to say what happens next," one said.
With Gulf gas oil prices 10 percent lower over the week because of a collapse in crude prices and Singapore products, some expect a modest price improvement to correct sharp losses.
Gulf crude premiums have also started to shake off some losses caused by weaker Asian import demand.
Omani premiums talked +10-15 cents from a low of +5-6 cents.
Murban for March delivery was assessed at a 20 cents premium to the ADNOC official price, down from a January high of +70-75, but expected to improve now it had hit a floor.
Premiums to independent price quotes for Gulf middle distillates have largely stayed resilient to the price dive with gas oil assessed at around 50-60 cents and jet at 60-65 cents.
"There is demand out there but buyers have waited for opportunities for lower prices." one trader said.
Gulf and east Africa product demand were said steady while Indian tender kerosene buying could provide support if the arbitrage from the Mediterranean was closed, traders said.
Cooler winter temperatures in the Gulf and neighbouring Iran has also kept some middle distillate supplies off the export market, traders said.
"Iran is keeping all its gas oil for local consumption," a trader said.
Gas oil was priced at $23.45 a barrel fob Gulf, a 10 cents improvement on the day but barely above their lowest level since August 1996.
Singapore middle distillate markets remained weak, pulled down by higher inventories and absent Chinese buying.
Demand for jet-kerosene was steadier and helped by Indonesian buying, pulling the spread to weak gas oil out to $3.00, compared to 85 cents for December.
